`@xandreed/process-host` is a Node 24 and Bun binding for running an agent in a
child process. The host supplies its Agent or TurnRunner, model, services and
entry module. A parent can push messages at any time through stdio NDJSON.
The package supplies protocol version 1, `StdioPeerLive`, `serveProcess`,
`runProcessHost` and the shipped `processPeerConformance` kit.

The [version 1 fixture](https://github.com/xandreeddev/efferent/blob/main/packages/process-host/fixtures/protocol-1.ndjson)
contains every command, event and progress variant. Later decoders continue to
decode it. The [shared subprocess journey](https://github.com/xandreeddev/efferent/blob/main/scripts/process-host-consumer.fixture.mjs)
runs against source Bun and packed Node/Bun packages, with independent journal
reads, SIGTERM, SIGKILL, retained inputs and actual blocked native output.

## Host entry

The entry calls `runProcessHost`. Its scoped `setup` factory constructs the
application's services after version negotiation. Use `serveProcess` when an
embedding host owns process lifetime and supplies its own ProcessPeer.

```ts
import { runProcessHost } from "@xandreed/process-host"
import type { ProcessHostOptions } from "@xandreed/process-host"

declare const setup: ProcessHostOptions["setup"]

await runProcessHost({ owners: ["my-app"], setup })
```

Setup receives `observe.sessionLog(inner)` and `observe.turnRunner(inner)`.
Wrap the exact logical SessionLog before constructing Sessions, outside any
media-store decoration, and use the observed TurnRunner for direct turns,
`agentInboxRunner` and `agentTaskExecutor`. The returned ProcessBinding holds:

| Field | Host supplies |
| --- | --- |
| `runner`, `use` | The shared observed runner and turn policy |
| `services` | Captured services for that runner, including its model and Sessions |
| `sessions` | The same Sessions used by every turn and drainer |
| `tasks` | `Option.some(Tasks)` when helper answers are supported |
| `activity`, `shutdown` | Effects captured over the complete shared activity/shutdown services |

Activity contains session IDs without owner fields. Capture the same owner
scope that the process exposes. Agent activity sees services built into the
agent; services supplied only per turn need the complete captured context for
`processActivity` and `shutdownGracefully`.

The factory creates sessions and chooses storage, model services, task runners
and the existing inbox drainer. It also owns explicit known-dead startup
recovery. Perform any `Tasks.reconcile(..., {takeOver:true})` under exclusive
startup authority before enabling competing local work. Reconcile can schedule
unrun tasks immediately, so a host that stages recovery must gate its supplied
TaskRunner as well as delay drainer activation. A new process connection alone
does not grant takeover authority. The shared journey demonstrates explicit
`begin.takeOver` after its parent witnesses SIGKILL.

## Handshake and framing

The first input frame is:

```json
{"_tag":"hello","requestId":"hello-1","protocolVersion":1}
```

The child replies with the same tag, request ID and supported version. This
acknowledges version negotiation; setup runs next and the reader processes work
commands when setup returns. Setup recovery may emit observed events after the
handshake. A version mismatch or a first command other than hello fails before
setup. A second hello and a duplicate outstanding request ID are fatal protocol
errors. Request IDs use 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `:`, or `-`.

Each frame is one UTF-8 JSON value followed by LF. CRLF is accepted. Blank
lines, leading BOMs, invalid UTF-8, malformed/schema-invalid JSON, excess command
properties and a nonempty unterminated final line fail the connection. Clean
EOF after negotiation starts graceful shutdown; EOF before hello is a protocol
failure. Every event is encoded through its schema before writing.

## Commands

Every command includes `_tag` and `requestId`. A session address is
`{id,owner}`; `id` is the existing conversation UUID. A UserMessage contains
`text` and `attachments`. The owner must be configured on the host before a
session command can touch its services.

| Command | Additional fields | Meaning of its reply |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `begin` | `session`, `runId`, `userMessage`; optional `key`, `command`, `meta`, `resumes`, `takeOver`, `timeLimitMs` | `begin.result` is the real TurnRunner result after its owned turn returns. Begin refusals produce a command error. |
| `send` | `session`, `input:{id,userMessage,source}` | `queued` acknowledges `Sessions.enqueue` with delivery `next`. |
| `steer` | Same input as send | `queued` acknowledges delivery `steer`; the next eligible step takes it, or it remains for a later turn. |
| `answer` | `parent`, `taskId`, `questionId`, `text` | `answered` preserves `Tasks.answer`'s `accepted:true` and `enqueued`. |
| `cancel` | `session`, `turn` | `cancelled` reports exact-turn cancellation and pending count. |
| `ping` | None | `pong` carries actual ProcessActivity. |
| `shutdown` | Optional `deadlineMs` within the host maximum | One graceful shutdown emits its report and flushes output. |

`begin.takeOver:true` is the parent host's explicit assertion that the old
holder is gone. It is never inferred or enabled by default. `resumes` keeps the
existing user-turn resume rules. The host provides session creation; a missing
session remains missing.

Stable turn keys, queued input IDs and question IDs provide durable idempotence.
A request ID only correlates a currently outstanding command and can be reused
after its response. Changing a queued input's message, delivery or source under
the same ID conflicts, even after consumption. A queue acknowledgment proves
storage acceptance. An answer with `enqueued:false` can be durably deferred by
a full inbox, or be an exact historical duplicate; it does not claim delivery.

The dispatcher runs begins independently from short commands and keeps a
separate control lane for cancel, ping and shutdown. Saturation returns
`host.busy` before executing that command. Tasks are optional; answer returns
`host.unsupported` when the binding has none. There are no implicit session,
history, task-start or task-status commands.

## Events and evidence

| Event | Payload |
| --- | --- |
| `hello` | Negotiated version and request ID |
| `turn.started` | Session/turn/run identity, origin, optional input/task/resume identity and journal `{seq,at}` |
| `turn.event` | Session/turn/run identity and `progress:{mode,event}` |
| `turn.ended` | Session/turn identity, reason, optional failureCode and journal cursor |
| `begin.result` | Outcome, reply, usage and optional pending count |
| `queued`, `answered`, `cancelled` | Their command's exact service result |
| `pong` | Activity, including distinct `inFlight` and `busy` |
| `shutdown` | ShutdownReport; signal/EOF shutdown can omit request ID |
| `error` | Owned code/message, fatal flag, optional request ID/frameworkCode |

Start/end frames follow successful logical SessionLog commit acknowledgments.
They cover direct, queued, initial task and parent-reaction turns. A prepared
bus outcome, Agent return or reply row cannot supply a durable end. Waiting is
a yielded turn, with a later helper answer starting a separate turn.

Lifecycle frames carry no admitted user message, metadata or failure message.
Their mandatory identity is `(session,turn)` plus the journal cursor; a stored
end has no run ID. Request ID is included when the live host knows it. Delayed
storage acknowledgments can arrive out of sequence, including an end before a
held start acknowledgment. Consumers use journal cursors rather than assuming
cross-session ordering or unconditional live start-before-end order.

A successful commit receipt remains successful if subsequent event forwarding
fails; the host records the peer failure and stops. A lost commit acknowledgment
can leave a durable row without a live frame, and a lost output acknowledgment
can leave a frame already received by the parent. This stream observes one
connection. Restart and retries use the durable journal and framework keys.

## Progress modes

`events:"projection"` is the default. It includes step state, assistant text
and text deltas, tool identity/status, safe refusal reasons and a fallback
marker. Tool status-channel text is included. Arguments, results, reasoning,
tool-parameter deltas, raw host/context/decision/interceptor payloads and
provider failure text are omitted.

`events:"full"` exports every non-lifecycle TurnEvent through its encoded JSON
shape. This includes structured tool results and their question IDs, which a
host rendering helper questions can use for `answer`. Full export snapshots
data without inherited JSON hooks, validates strict JSON and fails with an
owned error for unsupported values such as BigInt, cycles or functions. A
non-JSON decoded tool result can therefore require projection mode. Native
codec limits can reject extremely deep objects. Values are never silently
clipped into a different event.

## Bounds and shutdown

| Option | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `maxFrameBytes` | 24 MiB, excluding LF and optional CR |
| `readChunkBytes` | 64 KiB |
| `maxPendingWrites` | 64 |
| `writeTimeoutMs` | 10,000 |
| `maxBegins` / `maxShortCommands` / `controlCapacity` | 8 / 32 / 8 |
| `handshakeTimeoutMs` | 10,000 |
| `shutdown.deadlineMs` / `shutdown.reserveMs` | 25,000 / 2,000 |
| `hardDeadlineMs` on runProcessHost | 30,000 from the first stopping trigger |

The peer pulls input with one bounded partial frame and native chunk, without
a command queue. Pending writers reserve finite slots before encoding; one
writer snapshots and serializes at a time. Flush waits for all accepted native
write acknowledgments, including callers paused before taking the serial
permit. The first output failure remains visible to later sends and flush.
Schema serialization materializes one host event before checking its encoded
size, so a very large host object can temporarily exceed the frame byte budget.
The limit bounds accepted frames and owned input accumulation, rather than
total process memory. Disposing a peer removes its own listeners and workers
while leaving injected native streams open.

Graceful shutdown refuses new work, uses the binding's shutdown budget, then
interrupts remaining command workers when the remaining response allowance expires.
Accepted queue entries remain durable. A busy report can still include backlog
after active execution ends. Output acknowledgment has its own timeout.

`runProcessHost` routes default Effect logging to stderr and reserves stdout
for protocol frames. Host custom logging keeps that separation. The first
SIGINT/SIGTERM starts graceful shutdown; a second signal exits immediately.
An independent native timer runs outside Effect finalizers and bounds stuck
asynchronous setup, work, writes or teardown. A forced exit can truncate output.
JavaScript timers still require the event loop to run; an external supervisor
can SIGKILL synchronously blocked code.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Explicit shutdown or clean EOF, after successful flush |
| 1 | Configuration, setup, runtime, storage or output failure |
| 2 | Malformed input, handshake, version or sequencing failure |
| 124 | Independent hard deadline |
| 130 / 143 | SIGINT / SIGTERM, including a successfully handled first signal |

`serveProcess` returns a typed result/error and leaves native exit to its caller.
The process protocol version is independent of stored journal format. This
binding adds no stored shape, package release, provider configuration or UI.
